Diffing the same extraction at 2b76db076 against its parent gives exactly 36 changed rules and no others. In the running DB no rule from the change set is left in 'Monitoring' or 'Uncategorized': the only two 'Monitoring' rows are a-preop-pt-inr and a-preop-ptt (both untouched by the commit, both genuinely lab-monitoring rules), and the 8 remaining 'Uncategorized' rows (i-fluid-infusion-medication, i-last-local-anesthetic, i-latest-glucose, i-latest-medication, w-antibiotic-previous-doses, w-calcium-blood-transfusion, w-fluconazole-slow-administer, w-weight-type-adjustment) are all outside the change set. 'Diabetes Management' contains exactly the 13 moved insulin/glucose rules and nothing else. w-dantrolene-default-dose reads 'Wrong Dose', matching the commit message's note that PR #4341 already moved it, so this commit correctly leaves it alone.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix code in the container. First added /config/application.properties with logging.level.org.hibernate.orm.jdbc.bind=TRACE so the boot-time INSERT into rule_definitions logs its bound values, restarted, and confirmed the shipped build binds [Diabetes Management] (52 times = 13 rules x 4 tenants) and [Warns if cefazolin is selected ...] at 18:36, with zero occurrences of the pre-fix cefazolin wording. Then took the built SHA's source for all 36 changed files, reverse-applied the OR-2755 hunks (4 files needed the revert by hand because later commits moved them), compiled all 36 in-container with the app's own classpath plus lombok (javac exit 0, 41 class files), backed up /app/classes, copied the pre-fix classes in and restarted. The app booted cleanly - no boot failure, the new DIABETES_MANAGEMENT enum constant was left in place precisely so the pre-fix classes would load - and went red: rule_definitions in demo-demo differed from the shipped baseline in exactly 36 rows, 'Diabetes Management' dropped to 0 rows, 'Uncategorized' rose 8 -> 31, 'Monitoring' rose 2 -> 15, a-preop-glucose read 'Monitoring' and w-cefazolin-anaphylaxis-unknown-pen-allergy read 'Uncategorized'; all 36 matched the pre-fix source exactly. Restored /app/classes from the backup, verified all 41 class files match the shipped originals by md5, restarted: rule_definitions is byte-identical to the pre-red baseline dump, the API is back to 'Warns if cefazolin ...', the post-fix binding reappears at 18:41:35, and no boot failure. caveats: The ticket's only stated requirement is the attached guidance_categories_rules_updated.csv, which is not available in this environment; the shipped mapping was verified against the merged commit's intent, not against that CSV row by row.

The downstream consumers are Metabase queries over rollup matviews (guidance_category_breakdown_by_month, shared_error_count_by_category, error_rate_wrong_dose_by_medication) and none of those are reachable from this instance, so only the rule_definitions column they join was exercised.
As the commit message notes, these joins are live, so past firings are re-attributed too: previously published Monitoring and Uncategorized breakdowns will not reconcile with a re-run.

No analytics SQL hardcodes a category list, so 'Diabetes Management' needs no query change, but error_rate_wrong_dose_by_medication.sql does match the literal 'Wrong Dose', so friendly names are effectively part of the analytics contract.

automation.assessment: There is no coverage at all today. GuidanceCategory appears in only four test files and always as UNCATEGORIZED on a hand-rolled stub annotation; nothing asserts a real rule's category, nothing guards against a new rule shipping uncategorized, and nothing pins the friendly-name strings that the analytics SQL matches on. This recategorization is exactly the kind of change that silently regresses, so a checked-in expected mapping is worth locking in.
proposed_tests: Unit test that scans every @RuleDefinition-annotated class and asserts the full rule-id -> GuidanceCategory mapping against a checked-in expected table, so any future recategorization has to be deliberate.
Unit test asserting no rule declares GuidanceCategory.UNCATEGORIZED outside a small explicit allow-list, so a new rule cannot quietly land in the Uncategorized bucket.

Unit test pinning GuidanceCategory.getFriendlyName() for every constant and asserting uniqueness, since analytics SQL filters on the literal 'Wrong Dose' and a rename would silently empty a published metric.
Repository-level test that after startup sync, rule_definitions.guidance_category is non-null for every row and equals the annotation's friendly name.

Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: All 36 recategorized rules were read back from rule_definitions on a throwaway build of main, in all four tenant schemas, with Diabetes Management now holding exactly the 13 insulin and glucose rules.

Negative: Scraping every rule annotation at the built commit and comparing row by row showed no other rule moved, and the only remaining Monitoring rows are the two coagulation lab rules.

Red check: The pre-fix versions of all 36 rule classes were compiled and swapped into the running container, which sent Diabetes Management to zero rows and Uncategorized from 8 to 31, then the shipped classes were restored and verified.

Automation: There is no test asserting any rule's guidance category today, so a mapping test plus an uncategorized guard is proposed.
